must_do: run before any change exists — reconnaissance is not a change and produces no spec
interview the user for the frame instead of inferring the domain from the app name or the repo
produce two levels: Features (selectable, each one /opsx-propose change = one feature/ module) with FDD-granular Functions (`<action> the <result> <object>`) nested under them
ask the user to select at the FEATURE level, not the function level
write exactly two files — openspec/domain/model.md (coarse living vocabulary) and openspec/domain/features.md (candidate list) — and nothing else
stop at the three checkpoints R1 (frame), R2 (areas + concepts + archetypes), R3 (feature list), all gating
state in features.md that it is a one-time artifact and historical after a feature is selected
record open questions with the assumption taken wherever the brief is vague
must_not: emit SHALL/MUST or acceptance criteria — recon output is hypotheses, not requirements
produce an FDD-granular list as the selectable unit (too small to be a change in this kit)
choose architecture, modules, DTOs, screens, or a task breakdown — that is the change's job
write a spec, a change, or code
keep features.md updated after selection, or treat it as a second backlog
resolve a vague answer by inventing concepts rather than recording an open question

pass_criteria: openspec/domain/model.md and openspec/domain/features.md exist; the list is selectable at feature granularity with functions nested; no SHALL/MUST anywhere; all three checkpoints were presented and approved; the artifact states it is a one-time, unmaintained output.

should: where do I start on a new project
should_not: model the domain for the leaderboard change
